current_defensible_claim: Held-out GNSS receiver clocks contain operationally useful spatial structure, and the precise-clock TEP-scale fit is robust across five filters including detrend-only data. A phase/coherence prior frozen from the preceding day converts the Papers 1-2 phase-cos observable into causal outage skill: across 45 days it improves on distance-only TEP by 2.6-17.1%, causal CV spatial prediction by 4.8-23.4%, and a coherence-magnitude-preserving phase scramble by 14.4-37.2%, with positive clustered intervals. Co-located quartz/free-atomic anchors now convert that phase structure into spatial predictive power: two independent sites recover 3,282/3,732 km under station-clustered geometry nulls (p=0.001 each), and a target-blind 43-mode inversion localises Matera/Tahiti to 339/744 km versus 9,078/10,044 km null medians. This is a GNSS-derived observability replay; the live zero-satellite test requires direct local dual-clock phase measurements. Full-sky 3-D RMS is the wrong scoreboard for a time field: with 8 satellites geometry already estimates the receiver clock, so TEP is correctly inert in position (Step 23). Predictive power is in held-out clocks (P1, S6) and in dropout PPP (P3). At k=3 free-clock SPP is infeasible and TEP supplies the clock measurement. Phase-resolved k=3: RMS 5.75 m (p50 3.05 m) vs AR1 5.53 m / 2.83 m. The dense-network clock advantage (Step 55 p50 vs temporal: +6.2 to +19.3%) was previously discarded by a change-on-stale-SPP-anchor predictor; the flagship now injects the Step 55/56 absolute residual (trend + kriged live reference residuals) at 1 h and 4 h. Repeated one-millisecond wrap-mode targets are now rejected causally; unexpected steering still requires steering-event telemetry or an independent motion/position constraint. The temporal T4 regression breaks the co-visibility collinearity: with the corrected pooled common-view slope on real-SP3 co-visibility, the non-common-view component of pair correlation meets the frozen separability criterion on the broadcast product (PC=-0.164 > 0.15 at 10.8 sigma, OOS R^2 gain +0.022 > 0.02, lambda=1008 km) and shows a significant but attenuated partial correlation on the precise product (PC=-0.040, 9.2 sigma) -- the expected attenuation where the network solution absorbs the field's common mode and atomic oscillators screen the remainder. S2 is PARTIAL. An unconstrained Gaussian process resolves the TEP-predicted scale when the signal is present: with a noise-dominating injection it recovers the full TEP band at 88% within 2x (5/5 scales), the >1,000 km baseline-restricted free GP selects a 1,500 km median (85% in the TEP band), and both spatial-signal nulls collapse to the grid edge (0% of temporal-shuffle and 3% of geometry-shuffle nulls in the TEP band). At the real sub-noise amplitude SNR the band-passed-amplitude free GP picks ~700 km; the operative unconstrained-discovery evidence is the phase observable (S4: free form and free length scale, Gaussian at lambda in [3,820, 4,348] km on both precise centres). Operational robustness PASSES all 8 of 8 aperture dimensions (network density, pre-window, oscillator type, independent year, clock-filter family, corrupt-reference rejection, frozen live stream, and multi-region seasonal sweep across 30/30 region-season cells) with the prior frozen and physics-fixed.

D_synchronization_holonomy.criterion: the distinctive TEP observable: residual synchronization holonomy over a closed loop (non-exact/disformal sector), realised as the carrier-phase double difference, regressed on the signed loop invariant with co-located zero-area controls

corrections_applied: antenna PCO+PCV from igs20_2317.atx (0 uncorrected observations)
step68.interpretation: Properly controlled test of the NON-EXACT (disformal) TEP sector via the closed synchronization loop A->sat1->B->sat2->A, i.e. the double difference. Co-located controls are null as required (WTZR-WTZZ, identical LEIAR25.R3 antennas, z=+1.1). A significant direction-dependent term survives tropospheric-gradient and antenna PCV correction, but it does NOT carry the holonomy signature: the flux must scale with enclosed loop area, and |slope| vs baseline gives Spearman -0.14 while |slope| vs the pair's own DD noise gives +0.89. The term therefore tracks site-specific systematics (multipath, which ANTEX cannot remove since it is an antenna-model average, not a site calibration), not loop geometry. NO evidence for a non-exact sector at the 10-150 mm DD-residual level; any holonomy lies below the multipath floor. THIS DOES NOT BEAR ON THE SCALAR SECTOR, which is established (Papers 1-2 distance-structured cos-phase correlation; reproduced here at 27 sigma in Step 53, and operationally exploited in the Step 64 P1 pass).
step68.next_discriminator: Sidereal-day multipath stacking: GPS geometry repeats every 23h56m04s, so multipath repeats with it while a proper-time field effect does not. Stack N days aligned to sidereal time and subtract to suppress multipath by sqrt(N), then re-test the area scaling.

step69_sidereal.interpretation: MULTIPATH CHARACTERISATION ONLY. 96.7% (median) of the double-difference residual variance is sidereal-repeating, i.e. multipath: leave-one-day-out sidereal cleaning drops the DD residual from 79-145 mm to 13-31 mm. That part stands. The post-cleaning holonomy slopes (|z| <= 1.6) are NOT a bound on the non-exact sector and must not be reported as one: the loop invariant T is a function of satellite geometry, and satellite geometry is exactly what repeats every sidereal day, so the template removes a static geometry-locked signal along with the multipath. step_72 shows by injection that a static holonomy is recovered at 1.00 of its true slope before cleaning and 0.00 after, on all eight pairs, while a day-modulated injection survives at 1.26. The non-exact sector is therefore UNTESTED on this dataset, not bounded. Separating it requires a site-frame azimuth/elevation multipath model (multipath is a per-satellite, per-site function of az/el; T is an irreducibly two-satellite cross-product), not day-repetition.
step69_sidereal.prior_interpretation_withdrawn: DECISIVE. 96.7% (median) of the double-difference residual variance is sidereal-repeating, i.e. multipath: leave-one-day-out sidereal cleaning drops the DD residual from 79-145 mm to 13-31 mm. After t...

step72_template_blindness.interpretation: The leave-one-day-out sidereal template removes 100% of the holonomy regressor T itself, because T is a function of satellite geometry and GPS geometry is what repeats every sidereal day. A synthetic STATIC holonomy injected into the real double difference is recovered at 1.00 of its true slope before cleaning but only 0.00 after -- while a day-modulated injection survives at 1.26. Step 69's post-cleaning null is therefore NOT a bound on a static non-exact sector: the cleaning removes any geometry-locked signal along with the multipath. Step 69's 96.7% figure remains valid as a MULTIPATH characterisation; its holonomy null bounds only a day-to-day-VARYING component.

D_synchronization_holonomy.scope: Tests the sector the scalar cannot reach: a conformal-only field gives closed-loop integral of d ln A = 0 identically. Controls null as required. After tropospheric-gradient and ANTEX PCV correction a significant direction-dependent term remains, but it fails the decisive holonomy signature -- |slope| vs baseline rho = -0.14 whereas |slope| vs the pair's own DD noise rho = +0.89, i.e. site multipath, not loop area. No non-exact sector detected above the multipath floor. Step 69 measured the nuisance: 96.7% of the DD residual variance is sidereal-repeating multipath, and leave-one-day-out cleaning drops it 79-145 mm -> 13-31 mm. That multipath figure stands. Its post-cleaning holonomy null does NOT: step_72 shows by injection that the sidereal template removes a STATIC geometry-locked signal along with the multipath (the loop invariant T is a function of satellite geometry, and satellite geometry is what repeats every sidereal day). A synthetic static holonomy is recovered at 1.00 of its true slope before cleaning and 0.00 after, on all eight pairs, while a day-modulated one survives at 1.26. The correct separation is the site-frame az/el multipath model (multipath is a per-satellite per-site function of az/el while T is an irreducibly two-satellite cross-product): Step 79 fits per-station az/el surfaces jointly with T, recovers an injected static holonomy at 1.00 on all eight pairs (vs 0.00 for the sidereal template), and finds NO area-scaling holonomy (slope-vs-baseline Spearman -0.05; the residual detections track site systematics). The non-exact sector is therefore bounded by an estimator with demonstrated power. Independent of, and does not bear on, the established scalar-sector result (Papers 1-2; Step 53 at 27 sigma; Step 64 P1 statistical tie)

D_position_from_the_clock.criterion: measure the proper-time field's spatial gradient and test whether v.grad(phi) clears the measured clock-rate floor for any platform

metric.bottom_line: NULL RESULT, with a clear physical cause. The proper-time field is SMOOTH. The direct v.grad(phi) regression on GPS satellite clocks moving at 3.9 km/s returns a null (R^2 = 0.093 against a 0.125 noise expectation; recovered gradient vector temporally incoherent at 0.028, sign-flip null z = -0.1), bounding |grad phi| <= 1.7e-8 m/m at orbital altitude -- ~100x below the ground bound. Evaluating each platform at its own altitude's gradient, no platform clears 3x the measured clock-rate floor (4.1e-4 m/s): aircraft reach 1.3x, a road vehicle 0.15x, and an orbiting platform 0.4x because the field is so much smoother up there. Position-from-the-clock is therefore NOT available in this data. The reason matters: smoothness is exactly what makes the network predict a station's clock so well, so the property that powers Steps 55/56/64 is the same one that forecloses positioning. The only remaining window is fine structure below ~150 km, which no current product can resolve -- IGS clock products have almost no pairs there and SPP-derived dense products carry a 4-7 m noise floor. A dense CORS cluster processed with precise ephemerides would close it.

D_position_from_the_clock.scope: SCALAR-SECTOR BOUND, not a TEP null. The framework states that a conformal-only scalar cannot generate the distinctive signature: the local-rate response is the exact form d ln A, and its closed-loop integral vanishes identically, so any loop test of the scalar gradient nulls by construction regardless of amplitude. What Step 66 delivers is an upper bound on the CONFORMAL sector: <= 1.0e-6 m/m on the ground (three independent routes) and <= 1.7e-8 m/m at orbital altitude. Those are noise-limited: the estimator floor is ~0.5 m (code) to 0.072 m (rough carrier phase), while ambiguity-resolved processing reaches 0.003 m, so the regime where a realistic gradient becomes visible was never entered. The distinctive TEP observable is the residual synchronization holonomy over a closed loop (non-exact/disformal sector) -- tested in Step 68, NOT here

D_oscillator_screening.criterion: quartz (OCXO) receiver clocks show a larger band-limited residual but a higher network-predictable fraction than atomic (H-maser/Cs) references -- the extra variation is field, not local noise

metric.note: normalised phase-cos coherence is marginally lower for quartz (-0.021) because it also carries more incoherent local noise; the operationally meaningful quantities -- held-out predictable fraction AND absolute predictable power -- both favour quartz strongly

D_oscillator_screening.scope: TEP-consistent: the atomic transition is more screened from the proper-time field. Quartz clocks carry ~1.9x more network-predictable clock power. D_common_mode_is_tep.criterion: characterisation: the network-mean (cluster-mean) band-limited clock correlation decays with inter-region separation at the TEP Gaussian length, on satellite-common-mode-removed precise products

metric.interpretation: The mean band-limited clock of one region correlates with the mean of another region, decaying with inter-region separation at a Gaussian length of ~2,000-3,000 km -- the TEP scale (Steps 53, 58) -- not separation-independent (which a datum / time-scale common mode would give). It survives on precise products, where the satellite-clock common mode is already removed. The network-mean 'common mode' is therefore substantially the TEP field itself: the operational skill measured against persistence / predict-zero (Steps 55, 58) is the TEP contribution, and the skill measured against a bulk mean is a lower bound that removes most of the field.

D_common_mode_is_tep.scope: network-mean clock decays at lambda ~ 2,944 km on precise products; the coherent signal is broadband and SUPPRESSED (0.78x) at the GPS orbital / semidiurnal period -- inconsistent with orbit error (would peak there) or tropospheric/tidal common mode (would peak at 24/12 h); length scale matches the constellation-independent satellite-side Step 36. Supports treating skill vs persistence/predict-zero (Steps 55, 58) as the TEP contribution; skill vs a bulk mean is a lower bound
